name: freelo-mcp

tools.name: get_projects
tools.description: Fetches your own active projects in Freelo. Returns only projects that you own (where you are the project owner). For a complete list including shared projects, use get_all_projects instead. This is the quickest way to get an overview of projects you directly manage.

tools.name: get_all_projects
tools.description: Fetches all projects in Freelo - both projects you own and projects shared with you. Supports pagination for large datasets. Use this when you need a comprehensive view of all accessible projects, including archived and template projects. For just your own projects, use get_projects for better performance.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Creates a new project in Freelo. Requires a project name and currency. Optionally, you can specify a project owner (defaults to current user). The project will be created in active state. Use create_project_from_template if you want to create from an existing template instead.

name.description: Project name - clear and descriptive name for the new project

currency_iso.description: Project currency code: CZK (Czech Koruna), EUR (Euro), or USD (US Dollar). This affects invoicing and budget features.

project_owner_id.description: Optional: User ID of project owner (numeric string like "12345"). If not specified, the current authenticated user becomes the owner. Get user IDs from get_users.

tools.name: get_project_details
tools.description: Fetches detailed information about a specific project, including workers, tasklists, custom fields, and project settings. Use this after get_projects or get_all_projects to dive deeper into a specific project. Essential for understanding project structure before creating tasks or managing workers.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get project IDs from get_projects, get_all_projects, or other project listing tools.

tools.name: archive_project
tools.description: Archives a project in Freelo. Archived projects are hidden from default views but remain accessible via get_archived_projects. All project data, tasks, and history are preserved. This is reversible - use activate_project to restore. Archiving is recommended over deletion for completed projects.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier to archive (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tools.name: activate_project
tools.description: Activates an archived project in Freelo. The project will become visible in default views again and all functionality will be restored. Use this to un-archive projects that were previously archived. Get archived project IDs from get_archived_projects.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier to activate (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Must be an archived project - get IDs from get_archived_projects.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Permanently deletes a project from Freelo. WARNING: This action is irreversible! All tasks, files, comments, and project data will be permanently lost. Consider using archive_project instead for completed projects to preserve data. Only use this when you are absolutely certain the project should be removed.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier to permanently delete (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). WARNING: This is irreversible - all project data will be lost! Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tools.name: get_invited_projects
tools.description: Fetches projects where you have been invited as a collaborator but are not the owner. Returns projects shared with you by other users. Supports pagination. This is useful for viewing projects you contribute to but don't directly manage. For your own projects, use get_projects.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Each page returns a batch of projects.

tools.name: get_archived_projects
tools.description: Fetches archived projects in Freelo. Archived projects are completed or inactive projects hidden from default views but with all data preserved. Use this to find project IDs for reactivation with activate_project or to access historical project data. Supports pagination.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Each page returns a batch of archived projects.

tools.name: get_template_projects
tools.description: Fetches project templates in Freelo. Templates are reusable project structures with predefined tasklists, tasks, and settings. Use this to find templates for creating new projects with create_project_from_template. Supports filtering by name, date, tags, users, and pagination.

tags.description: Filter by template tags (array of tag strings)

users_ids.description: Filter by user IDs who have access to templates (array of numeric strings)

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0

filters.description: Optional filters for refining template results

tools.name: get_user_projects
tools.description: Fetches all projects accessible to a specific user (by user ID). Returns projects the user owns or has been invited to. Useful for viewing another team member's workload or project portfolio. Supports filtering by project state (active/archived/finished), sorting, and pagination. Get user IDs from get_users first.

userId.description: Unique user identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get user IDs from get_users or get_project_workers.

states_ids.description: Filter by project state IDs: 1=active, 2=archived, 3=template, 4=finished. Example: [1,4] for active and finished projects.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0

tools.name: create_project_from_template
tools.description: Creates a new project from an existing template. The new project will inherit the template's structure including tasklists, tasks, custom fields, and default settings. This is much faster than creating a project manually when you have standardized project structures. Get template IDs from get_template_projects first.

templateId.description: Unique template project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get template IDs from get_template_projects.

name.description: Name for the new project - should be descriptive and unique

currency_iso.description: Optional: Project currency (CZK, EUR, or USD). If not specified, inherits from template.

projectData.description: Configuration data for the new project

tools.name: get_all_tasks
tools.description: Fetches all tasks across all projects with powerful filtering options. Supports 14 different filters including fulltext search, project/tasklist filtering, label filtering, date ranges, worker assignment, and pagination. This is the primary tool for finding tasks - essential for task management workflows. For tasks in a specific tasklist, use get_tasklist_tasks for simpler queries.

search_query.description: Fulltext search in task names (case insensitive, e.g., "bug fix" or "feature")

state_id.description: Filter by task state ID: 1=active, 2=finished. Use get_all_states for complete list.

projects_ids.description: Filter by project IDs (e.g., [197352, 198000]). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tasklists_ids.description: Filter by tasklist IDs (e.g., [12345, 67890]). Get from get_project_tasklists.

with_label.description: Include only tasks with this label name (case insensitive, e.g., "urgent", "bug"). Get labels from find_available_labels.

without_label.description: Exclude tasks with this label name (case insensitive). Useful for filtering out specific categories.

no_due_date.description: When true, returns only tasks without a due date. Useful for finding unscheduled work.

date_from.description: Start date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (e.g., "2025-10-01")

date_to.description: End date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (e.g., "2025-10-31")

due_date_range.description: Filter tasks with due dates within this range. Useful for deadline management.

finished_overdue.description: When true, returns only tasks finished after their due date (late completions). Good for performance tracking.

date_from.description: Start date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS

date_to.description: End date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS

finished_date_range.description: Filter by completion date range. Essential for reporting and retrospectives.

worker_id.description: Filter by assigned worker ID (numeric, e.g., 12345). Get worker IDs from get_project_workers or get_users.

p.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Critical for large task sets to avoid token limits.

filters.description: Optional filters - combine multiple for precise queries

tools.name: get_tasklist_tasks
tools.description: Fetches tasks from a specific tasklist within a project. Simpler than get_all_tasks when you already know the project and tasklist. Returns tasks sorted by priority by default. Use this when drilling down from project → tasklist → tasks hierarchy. For cross-project task searches or complex filtering, use get_all_tasks instead.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tasklistId.description: Unique tasklist identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_project_tasklists or get_tasklist_details.

orderBy.description: Sort by: "priority" (default, highest first), "name" (alphabetically), "date_add" (creation date), or "date_edited_at" (last modified)

order.description: Sort direction: "asc" (ascending/A-Z/oldest first) or "desc" (descending/Z-A/newest first). Default: "asc"

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Creates a new task in a specific tasklist within a project. The task is created in active state by default. You can optionally assign it to a worker, set a due date, and add a description. After creation, use edit_task for modifications, or create_subtask to add subtasks. For creating from templates, use create_task_from_template instead.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tasklistId.description: Unique tasklist identifier where the task will be created (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_project_tasklists.

name.description: Task name - clear and descriptive title (required, e.g., "Fix login bug" or "Design homepage mockup")

description.description: Optional: Detailed task description in plain text or markdown. Use for context, requirements, or acceptance criteria.

worker.description: Optional: User ID to assign the task to (numeric, e.g., 12345). Get from get_project_workers. Leave empty for unassigned.

dueDate.description: Optional: Due date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (e.g., "2025-10-15" or "2025-10-15 17:00:00")

tools.name: get_task_details
tools.description: Fetches complete details about a specific task including name, description, assignees, due date, priority, status, labels, custom fields, and metadata. Use this after finding tasks with get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks to get full information before editing or taking action. Essential for understanding task context.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks, get_tasklist_tasks, or after create_task.

tools.name: edit_task
tools.description: Updates an existing task with new information. You can modify any combination of name, assignment, due date, or priority. All fields are optional - only provide the fields you want to change. Get task details with get_task_details first to see current values. IMPORTANT: To update task description, use update_task_description instead - this endpoint does not support description updates.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier to update (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

worker.description: Optional: User ID to assign task to (numeric). Get from get_project_workers.

dueDate.description: Optional: New due date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS

taskData.description: Task update data - only include fields to change

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Permanently deletes a task from Freelo. WARNING: This is irreversible! All task data including description, comments, attachments, subtasks, and history will be lost. Consider using finish_task instead to mark tasks as complete while preserving history. Only use when you are absolutely certain the task should be removed.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier to permanently delete (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). WARNING: This is irreversible! Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

tools.name: finish_task
tools.description: Marks a task as finished/completed. The task will be moved to finished state, preserving all data and history. Finished tasks can be reactivated later with activate_task if needed. This is the standard way to complete tasks - much safer than delete_task. Essential for task workflow completion.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier to mark as finished (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

tools.name: activate_task
tools.description: Reactivates a finished task, moving it back to active state. Use this when a completed task needs to be reopened or when work needs to continue. The task will become visible in active task lists again. Get finished tasks with get_finished_tasks or filter get_all_tasks with state_id=2.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier to reactivate (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Must be a finished task - get from get_finished_tasks.

tools.name: get_finished_tasks
tools.description: Fetches completed/finished tasks from a specific tasklist. Returns tasks that have been marked as done with finish_task. Useful for reviewing completed work, generating reports, or finding tasks to reactivate. Optionally filter results with fulltext search. For finished tasks across all projects, use get_all_tasks with state_id=2 instead.

tasklistId.description: Unique tasklist identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_project_tasklists.

search_query.description: Optional: Fulltext search query to filter finished task names (case insensitive, e.g., "bug fix")

tools.name: move_task
tools.description: Moves a task from its current tasklist to a different tasklist. The target tasklist can be in the same project or a different project. Task data, comments, attachments, and history are preserved. Use this for reorganizing work or transferring tasks between project phases. The task ID remains the same after moving.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier to move (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

targetTasklistId.description: Unique identifier of destination tasklist (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Can be in same or different project. Get from get_project_tasklists.

tools.name: get_task_description
tools.description: Fetches only the description content of a task. More lightweight than get_task_details when you only need the description text. Useful for reading task details without fetching full task metadata. Descriptions can contain plain text or markdown formatting with requirements, acceptance criteria, or notes.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

tools.name: update_task_description
tools.description: Updates only the description of a task without affecting other task properties. More efficient than edit_task when only changing the description. Supports plain text or markdown. Use this to add context, requirements, acceptance criteria, or technical notes. Previous description is replaced completely.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

description.description: New description content in plain text or markdown. Replaces existing description completely. Use empty string to clear description.

tools.name: create_task_reminder
tools.description: Creates a reminder notification for a task that will be sent at the specified date/time. Users will receive notifications in Freelo to check the task. Useful for follow-ups, deadlines, or periodic reviews. You can remind specific users or use default assignees. Delete with delete_task_reminder if needed.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

date.description: Reminder date and time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2025-10-15T14:00:00Z" or "2025-10-15T14:00:00+02:00"). Users will be notified at this time.

user_ids.description: Optional: Array of user IDs to remind (e.g., ["12345", "67890"]). If not specified, task assignees are reminded. Get IDs from get_project_workers.

tools.name: delete_task_reminder
tools.description: Removes an existing reminder from a task. Use this to cancel scheduled reminders that are no longer needed or were set incorrectly. The task itself is not affected - only the reminder is removed. Users will no longer receive the scheduled notification.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Must have an existing reminder. Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

tools.name: get_public_link
tools.description: Generates or retrieves a public sharing link for a task. Anyone with this link can view the task details without logging into Freelo - useful for sharing with external stakeholders, clients, or contractors. The link remains active until deleted with delete_public_link. Task content is read-only via public links.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details. A public link will be generated if none exists.

tools.name: delete_public_link
tools.description: Removes the public sharing link for a task. After deletion, the previous link URL will no longer work and task details will no longer be accessible without authentication. Use this when you no longer want to share the task publicly or when project information becomes confidential. The task itself is not deleted.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Must have an existing public link. Get from get_all_tasks or after get_public_link.

tools.name: create_task_from_template
tools.description: Creates a new task based on an existing template task. The new task inherits the template's name, description, custom fields, subtasks, and structure. Saves time when creating repetitive tasks with standardized formats. Find templates in template projects using get_template_projects. After creation, you can modify the task with edit_task.

templateId.description: Unique template task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get template tasks from projects returned by get_template_projects.

projectId.description: Unique identifier of target project where task will be created (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tasklistId.description: Unique identifier of target tasklist where task will be created (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_project_tasklists.

tools.name: set_total_time_estimate
tools.description: Sets the total estimated time for completing a task in minutes. This is a PREMIUM FEATURE and may require a paid Freelo plan (returns 402 Payment Required on free plans). Estimates help with project planning, resource allocation, and deadline forecasting. Use set_user_time_estimate for per-user estimates instead. Delete with delete_total_time_estimate.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

minutes.description: Total estimated time in minutes (e.g., 60 for 1 hour, 480 for 8 hours, 120 for 2 hours). Must be positive number.

tools.name: delete_total_time_estimate
tools.description: Removes the total time estimate from a task. This is a PREMIUM FEATURE (may return 402 Payment Required on free plans). Use this when estimates are no longer needed or were set incorrectly. The task itself is not affected. Time tracking history is preserved.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Must have an existing total time estimate. Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

tools.name: set_user_time_estimate
tools.description: Sets a time estimate for a specific user on a task. This is a PREMIUM FEATURE (may return 402 Payment Required on free plans). Useful for collaborative tasks where different team members contribute different amounts of time. Each user can have their own estimate. Use set_total_time_estimate for overall task estimate instead. Delete with delete_user_time_estimate.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

userId.description: Unique user identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). User should be assigned to task or project. Get from get_project_workers.

minutes.description: Estimated time for this specific user in minutes (e.g., 120 for 2 hours, 60 for 1 hour). Must be positive number.

tools.name: delete_user_time_estimate
tools.description: Removes a user-specific time estimate from a task. This is a PREMIUM FEATURE (may return 402 Payment Required on free plans). Use this when a user's estimate is no longer needed or was set incorrectly. Other users' estimates and the task itself are not affected.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Must have an existing user time estimate. Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

userId.description: Unique user identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Must have an existing time estimate on this task. Get from get_project_workers.

tools.name: get_project_tasklists
tools.description: Fetches all tasklists within a project. Tasklists organize tasks into logical groups or phases (e.g., "To Do", "In Progress", "Done" or "Design", "Development", "Testing"). Essential for understanding project structure before creating or finding tasks. Use this after get_project_details to drill down into project organization.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects, get_all_projects, or get_project_details.

tools.name: create_tasklist
tools.description: Creates a new tasklist (task group) within a project. Tasklists help organize tasks into phases, sprints, or categories. Common examples: "Backlog", "Sprint 1", "Design Phase", "Bug Fixes". After creation, use create_task to add tasks. For creating from templates, use create_tasklist_from_template instead.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier where tasklist will be created (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

name.description: Tasklist name - clear and descriptive (e.g., "Sprint 1", "Design Phase")

description.description: Optional: Description of the tasklist purpose

color.description: Optional: Tasklist color as hex code (e.g., "#ff0000")

tools.name: get_tasklist_details
tools.description: Fetches detailed information about a specific tasklist including name, description, color, workers, and settings. Use this after get_project_tasklists to understand tasklist configuration before creating tasks or managing workers. Essential for understanding tasklist structure and permissions.

tasklistId.description: Unique tasklist identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_project_tasklists or get_all_projects.

tools.name: get_assignable_workers
tools.description: Fetches the list of users who can be assigned to tasks in a specific tasklist. This considers project permissions and tasklist worker restrictions. Use this before creating or assigning tasks to ensure the assignee has access. Returns user details including names, IDs, and availability.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tasklistId.description: Unique tasklist identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_project_tasklists.

tools.name: create_tasklist_from_template
tools.description: Creates a new tasklist based on an existing template tasklist. The new tasklist inherits the template's structure, tasks, and settings. Much faster than creating tasklists manually when you have standardized workflows. Find template tasklists in template projects using get_template_projects.

templateId.description: Unique template tasklist identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from tasklists in template projects returned by get_template_projects.

projectId.description: Unique identifier of target project where tasklist will be created (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tools.name: create_subtask
tools.description: Creates a subtask under an existing task. Subtasks help break down complex tasks into smaller, manageable pieces. Each subtask can have its own assignment, description, and due date. Useful for detailed task decomposition and better progress tracking. Use get_subtasks to list existing subtasks.

taskId.description: Unique parent task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). The subtask will be created under this task. Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

name.description: Subtask name - clear and actionable (e.g., "Write unit tests", "Review code", "Update documentation")

description.description: Optional: Detailed subtask description with context or requirements

worker.description: Optional: User ID to assign subtask to (numeric). Can be different from parent task assignee. Get from get_project_workers.

dueDate.description: Optional: Due date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS

tools.name: get_subtasks
tools.description: Fetches all subtasks belonging to a parent task. Returns a list of subtasks with their names, statuses, assignments, and due dates. Essential for understanding task breakdown and progress on complex tasks. Use this before marking tasks complete to ensure all subtasks are done.

taskId.description: Unique parent task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "25368707"). Returns all subtasks under this task. Get from get_all_tasks or get_task_details.

tools.name: create_comment
tools.description: Creates a new comment on a task. Comments are visible to all project members and support file attachments. Use this for discussions, feedback, or updates. For editing existing comments, use edit_comment. Get task IDs from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

content.description: Comment content - text of the comment (supports plain text and markdown)

fileUuids.description: Optional: Array of file UUIDs to attach to the comment. Get UUIDs from upload_file.

tools.name: edit_comment
tools.description: Edits an existing comment on a task. Only the comment author or project admin can edit comments. You can update the text content and modify attached files. Use get_all_comments to retrieve comment IDs. For creating new comments, use create_comment instead.

commentId.description: Unique comment identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_comments.

content.description: Updated comment content - new text for the comment (supports plain text and markdown)

fileUuids.description: Optional: Array of file UUIDs to attach (replaces existing attachments). Get UUIDs from upload_file.

tools.name: get_all_comments
tools.description: Fetches all comments across projects with filtering and sorting options. Comments include discussions on tasks, documents, files, and links. Essential for tracking communication, finding specific conversations, or generating activity reports. Supports filtering by project, comment type, and pagination.

projects_ids.description: Filter by project IDs (numeric array, e.g., [197352, 198000]). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

type.description: Filter by comment context: "all" (default, all comments), "task" (task comments), "document" (note comments), "file" (file comments), "link" (link comments)

order_by.description: Sort by: "date_add" (creation date, default), "date_edited_at" (last edited date)

order.description: Sort direction: "asc" (oldest first) or "desc" (newest first, default)

p.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Critical for large comment sets to avoid token limits.

tools.name: get_all_files
tools.description: Fetches all files and documents across projects with filtering options. Returns files, directories, links, and documents attached to tasks or uploaded to projects. Supports pagination for large file sets. Use this to find attachments, browse project files, or locate specific documents before downloading with download_file.

projects_ids.description: Filter by project IDs (e.g., [197352, 198000]). Get from get_projects. Omit to search all projects.

type.description: Filter by item type: "directory" (folders), "link" (URL links), "file" (uploaded files), "document" (documents). Omit for all types.

p.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Use for large file collections to avoid token limits.

filters.description: Optional filters - combine to narrow results

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Uploads a file to Freelo. The file can then be attached to tasks, comments, or stored in project files. Supports any file type. Files are encoded as base64 for transfer. After upload, use the returned file UUID with download_file or to attach to tasks. Maximum file size depends on Freelo plan.

fileData.description: File content encoded as base64 string. Convert file bytes to base64 before passing. Example in Node.js: Buffer.from(fileBytes).toString("base64")

fileName.description: Original filename with extension (e.g., "report.pdf", "screenshot.png", "document.docx"). Preserves file type and helps with identification.

tools.name: download_file
tools.description: Downloads a file from Freelo by its UUID. Returns the file content which can be saved locally or processed. Use this after finding files with get_all_files to retrieve the actual file data. The UUID is returned when uploading files or found in file listings.

fileUuid.description: Unique file identifier (UUID format, e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_all_files or after upload_file.

tools.name: get_users
tools.description: Fetches all users in the Freelo workspace. Returns complete user list with names, emails, IDs, roles, and availability. Essential for getting user IDs before assigning tasks, inviting to projects, or managing permissions. Use this as the first step when working with team members.

tools.name: remove_workers
tools.description: Removes team members from a project. Provide either userIds (array of user ID strings) or emails (array of email strings) - at least one is required. Workers will immediately lose access to the project and its tasks. Get user IDs from get_project_workers or get_users.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

userIds.description: Array of user IDs to remove (e.g., ["12345", "67890"]). Get user IDs from get_project_workers or get_users.

emails.description: Array of email addresses to remove (e.g., ["user@example.com"]). Get emails from get_project_workers.

tools.name: get_project_workers
tools.description: Fetches the list of workers (team members) assigned to a specific project. Returns user details including names, emails, roles, and permissions. Essential for understanding team composition before assigning tasks or managing project access.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Use for projects with many team members.

tools.name: invite_users
tools.description: Invites users to a project. Provide either userIds (array of existing user ID strings) or emails (array of email strings) - at least one is required. When using emails, users without Freelo accounts will receive invitation emails. Get user IDs from get_users.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

userIds.description: Array of user IDs to invite (e.g., ["12345", "67890"]). Users must already exist in Freelo. Get IDs from get_users.

emails.description: Array of email addresses to invite (e.g., ["user@example.com"]). Users will receive invitations if not registered.

tools.name: get_out_of_office
tools.description: Fetches out-of-office (vacation/absence) information for a user. Returns dates and reason if set. Useful for checking team member availability before assigning tasks or scheduling work.

userId.description: Unique user identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_users or get_project_workers.

tools.name: set_out_of_office
tools.description: Sets out-of-office (vacation/absence) period for a user. Other team members will see when the user is unavailable. Delete with delete_out_of_office to cancel.

userId.description: Unique user identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Typically the current user. Get from get_users.

date_from.description: Absence start date in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-10-15")

date_to.description: Absence end date in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-10-20"). Must be after date_from.

reason.description: Optional: Absence reason (e.g., "Vacation", "Sick leave"). Visible to team members.

tools.name: delete_out_of_office
tools.description: Removes out-of-office status for a user. The user will appear as available immediately.

userId.description: Unique user identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Must have existing out-of-office status. Get from get_users.

tools.name: get_project_manager_of
tools.description: Fetches projects where the current authenticated user is assigned as the project manager (PM). This differs from get_projects which returns projects you own - you can be PM on projects owned by others.

tools.name: start_time_tracking
tools.description: Starts real-time time tracking for a task or general work. Creates an active timer that runs until stopped with stop_time_tracking. Use this for live time tracking during work - when stopped, it automatically creates a work report. For manual time entry after work is done, use create_work_report instead.

taskId.description: Optional: Task ID to track time for (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). If not provided, tracks general work time. Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

tools.name: stop_time_tracking
tools.description: Stops the currently active time tracking session. Calculates elapsed time since start_time_tracking was called and automatically creates a work report with the tracked time. Use this when finishing work on a task. If no timer is running, this will return an error.

tools.name: edit_time_tracking
tools.description: Edits the currently active time tracking session. Use this to change which task is being tracked or add/update the description while the timer is still running. Useful when you realize you started tracking the wrong task or want to add notes. Only works with an active timer.

task_id.description: Optional: New task ID to track time for (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Use to switch task while timer runs.

description.description: Optional: Description to add to the time tracking session (e.g., "Working on feature X"). Will appear in work report when stopped.

trackingData.description: Data to edit in current time tracking - all fields optional

tools.name: get_work_reports
tools.description: Fetches work reports with powerful filtering options. Work reports track time spent on tasks - essential for billing, productivity analysis, and project reporting. Supports filtering by projects, users, task labels, and date ranges. Use this for generating timesheets, analyzing team productivity, or preparing client invoices.

projects_ids.description: Filter by project IDs (numeric strings, e.g., ["197352", "198000"]). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

users_ids.description: Filter by user IDs (numeric strings, e.g., ["12345", "67890"]). Get from get_users or get_project_workers.

tasks_labels.description: Filter by task label names (e.g., ["urgent", "bug"]). Get labels from find_available_labels.

date_reported_range.description: Filter by date range when work was reported. Essential for monthly/weekly reports.

filters.description: Optional filters - combine multiple for precise queries

tools.name: create_work_report
tools.description: Creates a new work report (time entry) for a specific task. Work reports track time spent on tasks for billing, productivity analysis, and project reporting. Use this after completing work on a task or at end of day for timesheet entry. For real-time tracking, use start_time_tracking instead.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks, get_tasklist_tasks, or get_task_details.

minutes.description: Number of minutes worked (e.g., 120 for 2 hours, 30 for half hour). Will be converted to hours in reports.

date.description: Date of work in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-10-11"). Usually today's date or past date for retroactive entries.

note.description: Optional: Note about work performed (e.g., "Fixed login bug", "Client meeting notes"). Useful for detailed billing and reporting.

tools.name: update_work_report
tools.description: Updates an existing work report. Use this to correct time entries, update descriptions, or change the date of logged work. Useful for fixing mistakes in timesheets or adding details to previously logged work. Get work report IDs from get_work_reports.

workReportId.description: Unique work report identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_work_reports response.

minutes.description: Optional: Updated number of minutes worked (e.g., 120 for 2 hours)

date.description: Optional: Updated date in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-10-11")

note.description: Optional: Updated note about work performed

reportData.description: Updated work report data - all fields optional, only provide what needs to change

tools.name: delete_work_report
tools.description: Permanently deletes a work report (time entry). WARNING: This action is irreversible! Use this to remove incorrect time entries or duplicate reports. Consider using update_work_report to fix mistakes instead of deleting. Get work report IDs from get_work_reports.

workReportId.description: Unique work report identifier to permanently delete (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). WARNING: This is irreversible! Get from get_work_reports response.

tools.name: get_custom_field_types
tools.description: Fetches all available custom field types in Freelo. Custom fields allow you to extend tasks with additional metadata like priority levels, client names, budget amounts, or any project-specific data. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Use this before create_custom_field to see available field types (text, number, date, select, etc.).

tools.name: create_custom_field
tools.description: Creates a new custom field for a project. Custom fields extend tasks with project-specific metadata (e.g., "Client Name", "Priority Level", "Budget"). PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. After creation, use add_or_edit_field_value to set values on tasks. Get field types from get_custom_field_types first.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

name.description: Name of the custom field (e.g., "Client Name", "Priority Level", "Budget Amount")

type.description: Type of the custom field (e.g., "text", "number", "date", "select"). Get available types from get_custom_field_types.

is_required.description: Whether field is required when creating/editing tasks: "yes" or "no" (default). Required fields must be filled in.

tools.name: rename_custom_field
tools.description: Renames an existing custom field. Use this to update the display name of a custom field across the entire project. All existing values are preserved, only the field label changes. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get custom field UUIDs from get_custom_fields_by_project.

uuid.description: UUID of the custom field to rename (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project response.

name.description: New name for the custom field (e.g., "Updated Priority Level", "New Client Field")

tools.name: delete_custom_field
tools.description: Deletes a custom field from a project. The field will be removed from all tasks and hidden from views. This is reversible - use restore_custom_field to un-delete. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get custom field UUIDs from get_custom_fields_by_project. Consider renaming instead if you might need it later.

uuid.description: UUID of the custom field to delete (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project response.

tools.name: restore_custom_field
tools.description: Restores a previously deleted custom field. The field will become visible again with all its values preserved. Use this to un-delete custom fields that were removed with delete_custom_field. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get deleted field UUIDs from get_custom_fields_by_project.

uuid.description: UUID of the deleted custom field to restore (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project response (includes deleted fields).

tools.name: add_or_edit_field_value
tools.description: Sets or updates a custom field value on a task. Use this to add metadata like client names, budgets, or priorities to tasks. For enum/select fields, use add_or_edit_enum_value instead. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Works with text, number, date, and other non-enum field types.

task_id.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks, get_tasklist_tasks, or get_task_details.

custom_field_uuid.description: UUID of the custom field (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project.

value.description: Value to set. Type depends on field: string for text, number for numeric, boolean for checkbox, "YYYY-MM-DD" for date.

tools.name: add_or_edit_enum_value
tools.description: Sets or updates an enum/select custom field value on a task. Use this for dropdown/select custom fields (e.g., "Priority: High/Medium/Low", "Status: Approved/Pending/Rejected"). For other field types, use add_or_edit_field_value instead. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get enum options from get_enum_options.

task_id.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

custom_field_uuid.description: UUID of the enum custom field (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project.

enum_option_uuid.description: UUID of the enum option to select (e.g., "b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f12345678901"). Get from get_enum_options.

tools.name: delete_field_value
tools.description: Deletes a custom field value from a task. Use this to clear/remove custom field data from a task. The custom field definition remains, only this specific task's value is removed. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get value UUIDs from task details or get_custom_fields_by_project response.

uuid.description: UUID of the field value to delete (e.g., "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-123456789012"). Get from task details in get_task_details response or get_custom_fields_by_project.

tools.name: get_custom_fields_by_project
tools.description: Fetches all custom fields defined in a specific project, including their UUIDs, types, and configurations. Essential for understanding which custom fields are available before setting values on tasks. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Returns both active and deleted fields.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects, get_all_projects, or get_project_details.

tools.name: get_enum_options
tools.description: Fetches all available options for an enum/select custom field. Use this to see what values can be selected before using add_or_edit_enum_value. Returns option UUIDs, names, and colors. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Only works with enum/select type fields.

customFieldUuid.description: UUID of the enum custom field (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project for enum-type fields.

tools.name: change_enum_option
tools.description: Renames an existing enum/select custom field option. Use this to update option labels without changing which tasks have it selected. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get option UUIDs from get_enum_options.

enumUuid.description: UUID of the enum option to rename (e.g., "b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f12345678901"). Get from get_enum_options.

value.description: New value/name for the option (e.g., "Critical Priority", "Approved")

tools.name: delete_enum_option
tools.description: Deletes an enum/select custom field option. Fails if the option is currently in use on any task. Use force_delete_enum_option to delete even if in use. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Get option UUIDs from get_enum_options.

enumUuid.description: UUID of the enum option to delete (e.g., "b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f12345678901"). Get from get_enum_options.

tools.name: force_delete_enum_option
tools.description: Force-deletes an enum/select custom field option even if it is currently in use on tasks. Tasks with this option will have the value cleared. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Use regular delete_enum_option first if unsure.

enumUuid.description: UUID of the enum option to force-delete (e.g., "b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f12345678901"). Get from get_enum_options.

tools.name: create_enum_option
tools.description: Creates a new option for an enum/select custom field. Use this to add new values to dropdown fields (e.g., add "Critical" to a "Priority" field). After creation, use add_or_edit_enum_value to assign this option to tasks. PREMIUM FEATURE: Requires paid Freelo plan. Only works with enum/select type fields.

customFieldUuid.description: UUID of the enum custom field (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_fields_by_project for enum-type fields.

name.description: Name of the new option (e.g., "High Priority", "Approved", "Phase 2"). Will appear in dropdown.

color.description: Optional: Color for the option in hex format (e.g., "#FF0000" for red, "#00FF00" for green). Used for visual distinction.

tools.name: get_issued_invoices
tools.description: Fetches issued invoices with filtering options. Use this to retrieve client invoices for accounting, billing reports, or financial analysis. Supports filtering by project and date range. Essential for tracking billable work and generating financial reports.

project_id.description: Filter by project ID (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

date_from.description: Filter invoices from this date in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-10-01")

date_to.description: Filter invoices to this date in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-10-31")

tools.name: get_invoice_detail
tools.description: Fetches detailed information about a specific invoice, including line items, work reports, amounts, and status. Use this to review invoice details before sending to clients or for detailed accounting records. Get invoice IDs from get_issued_invoices.

invoiceId.description: Unique invoice identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_issued_invoices response.

tools.name: download_invoice_reports
tools.description: Downloads work reports and time tracking data associated with an invoice. Use this to get detailed breakdown of billable work for client transparency or internal auditing. Returns work report data that was included in the invoice calculation.

invoiceId.description: Unique invoice identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_issued_invoices or get_invoice_detail.

tools.name: get_invoice_reports_json
tools.description: Fetches work reports associated with an invoice as structured JSON data (unlike download_invoice_reports which returns CSV). Returns detailed work report entries with project, tasklist, and user information. Ideal for programmatic processing of invoice data.

invoiceId.description: Unique invoice identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_issued_invoices or get_invoice_detail.

tools.name: mark_as_invoiced
tools.description: Marks an invoice as invoiced (sent to client). Use this to track invoice status and indicate that the invoice has been delivered to the client. Important for invoice lifecycle management and accounting workflows. Get invoice IDs from get_issued_invoices.

invoiceId.description: Unique invoice identifier to mark as invoiced (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_issued_invoices response.

tools.name: get_all_notifications
tools.description: Fetches all notifications for the current user. Notifications include mentions, task assignments, comments, and other activity updates. Supports pagination for large notification lists. Use this to build notification feeds or check for unread updates.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 1 (default: 1). Use for loading more notifications.

limit.description: Number of notifications per page (e.g., 20, 50). Use to control response size.

tools.name: mark_notification_read
tools.description: Marks a specific notification as read. Use this to track which notifications have been seen and reduce unread notification counts. Essential for notification management workflows. Get notification IDs from get_all_notifications.

notificationId.description: Unique notification identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_notifications response.

tools.name: mark_notification_unread
tools.description: Marks a specific notification as unread. Use this to flag notifications that require follow-up action or to restore notifications that were accidentally marked as read. Get notification IDs from get_all_notifications.

notificationId.description: Unique notification identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_notifications response.

tools.name: create_note
tools.description: Creates a new note in a project. Notes are standalone documents for project documentation, meeting minutes, specifications, or any reference material. Unlike task comments, notes are top-level project items. Use this for knowledge base, documentation, or project wikis.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

name.description: Title of the note (e.g., "Meeting Minutes 2025-10-11", "API Documentation", "Project Spec")

content.description: Content of the note in plain text or markdown. Can include detailed documentation, meeting notes, specifications, etc.

tools.name: get_note
tools.description: Fetches a specific note by ID, including its title, content, and metadata. Use this to read project documentation, meeting minutes, or reference materials. Get note IDs from project details or search results.

noteId.description: Unique note identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from create_note response or project details.

tools.name: update_note
tools.description: Updates an existing note's title or content. Use this to maintain documentation, update meeting minutes, or revise project specifications. All fields are optional - only provide what needs to change. Get note IDs from get_note or project details.

noteId.description: Unique note identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from create_note, get_note, or project details.

name.description: Optional: Updated title of the note

content.description: Optional: Updated content of the note in plain text or markdown

noteData.description: Updated note data - all fields optional, only provide what needs to change

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description: Permanently deletes a note from a project. WARNING: This action is irreversible! All note content will be permanently lost. Consider updating the note to archive it instead. Use this only when you are certain the note should be removed.

noteId.description: Unique note identifier to permanently delete (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). WARNING: This is irreversible! Get from create_note, get_note, or project details.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Fetches activity events (audit log) with powerful filtering options. Events track all changes in Freelo: task updates, comments, status changes, assignments, file uploads, etc. Essential for activity tracking, auditing, generating reports, or building activity feeds. Supports filtering by projects, users, event types, tasks, and date ranges with pagination.

projects_ids.description: Filter by project IDs (numeric array, e.g., [197352, 198000]). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

users_ids.description: Filter by user IDs who performed actions (numeric array, e.g., [12345, 67890]). Get from get_users.

events_types.description: Filter by event types (e.g., ["task_created", "task_finished", "comment_added"]). Common types: task_created, task_finished, task_assigned, comment_added, file_uploaded.

order.description: Sort order: "desc" (newest first, default) or "asc" (oldest first)

date_from.description: Start date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (e.g., "2025-10-01")

date_to.description: End date in format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (e.g., "2025-10-31")

date_range.description: Filter events within date range. Essential for period reports and historical analysis.

tasks_ids.description: Filter by task IDs (numeric array, e.g., [12345, 67890]). Use to see all activity for specific tasks.

p.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Critical for large event sets to avoid token limits.

filters.description: Optional filters - combine multiple for precise queries

tools.name: get_custom_filters
tools.description: Fetches all custom filters (saved task views) created by the user. Custom filters are saved search configurations that combine multiple criteria for quick access to specific task sets. Use this to get filter UUIDs before using get_tasks_by_filter_uuid or get_tasks_by_filter_name.

tools.name: get_tasks_by_filter_uuid
tools.description: Fetches tasks using a custom filter UUID. Custom filters are pre-configured task searches with multiple criteria. Use this to quickly retrieve task sets matching saved filter configurations. Get filter UUIDs from get_custom_filters.

uuid.description: UUID of the custom filter (e.g., "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"). Get from get_custom_filters response.

tools.name: get_tasks_by_filter_name
tools.description: Fetches tasks using a custom filter name. Alternative to get_tasks_by_filter_uuid when you know the filter name but not the UUID. Custom filters are pre-configured task searches. Get filter names from get_custom_filters.

name.description: Name of the custom filter (e.g., "My High Priority Tasks", "Overdue Items"). Get from get_custom_filters response.

tools.name: find_available_labels
tools.description: Fetches all available task labels (tags) in Freelo, optionally filtered by project. Labels are used to categorize and filter tasks (e.g., "urgent", "bug", "feature", "design"). Essential before using get_all_tasks with label filters or when applying labels to tasks. Returns label names, colors, and usage counts.

projectId.description: Optional: Project ID to get project-specific labels (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). If omitted, returns all labels across all projects. Get from get_projects.

tools.name: add_labels_to_task
tools.description: Adds one or more labels to a task. Labels are used for categorizing and filtering tasks (e.g., "bug", "urgent", "feature"). Multiple labels can be added at once. Use find_available_labels to discover available label UUIDs. For removing labels, use remove_labels_from_task.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

labelIds.description: Array of label IDs to add (e.g., [28279, 28280]). Get label IDs from find_available_labels.

tools.name: remove_labels_from_task
tools.description: Removes one or more labels from a task. This is useful for cleaning up task categorization or removing outdated labels. Multiple labels can be removed at once. Only labels currently attached to the task can be removed. For adding labels, use add_labels_to_task.

taskId.description: Unique task identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks or get_tasklist_tasks.

labelIds.description: Array of label IDs to remove (e.g., [28279, 28280]). Must be labels currently attached to this task.

tools.name: edit_label
tools.description: Edits an existing project label (name, color, or visibility). Use this to update label properties without removing it from tasks. Get label IDs from find_available_labels.

labelId.description: Unique label identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from find_available_labels.

color.description: Label color in hex format from allowed set: #77787a, #15acc0, #367fee, #10aa40, #f2830b, #ca3e99, #9235e4, #e9483a, #ffffff, #e3b51e, #e8384f, #fd612c, #fda41a, #f4bd38, #a4c61a, #62d26f, #37a862, #159ddc, #4186e0, #7a6ff0, #aa62e3, #e362e3, #ea4e9d, #fc91ad, #8da3a6, #e9e9e9

is_private.description: Whether label is private (visible only to you). Defaults to false.

labelData.description: Label update data - name and color are required by API

tools.name: delete_label
tools.description: Deletes a project label permanently. The label will be removed from all tasks that have it. This action cannot be undone. Get label IDs from find_available_labels.

labelId.description: Unique label identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from find_available_labels.

tools.name: add_label_to_project
tools.description: Adds an existing label to a project, making it available for tasks in that project. Use this to share labels across projects or associate a label with a specific project.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects.

id.description: ID of an existing label to add. If omitted, creates a new label.

labelData.description: Label data to add to the project

tools.name: remove_label_from_project
tools.description: Removes a label from a project. The label will no longer be available for tasks in this project but still exists globally. Use find_available_labels to get label details.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects.

id.description: ID of the label to remove from the project. Get from find_available_labels.

labelData.description: Label data to remove from the project

tools.name: create_task_labels
tools.description: Creates a new task label (tag) for categorizing tasks. Labels help organize and filter tasks across projects (e.g., "urgent", "bug", "feature", "design"). After creation, labels can be applied to tasks via edit_task or filtered with get_all_tasks. Use find_available_labels to see existing labels first.

name.description: Name of the label (e.g., "urgent", "bug", "feature", "design"). Should be short and descriptive for easy filtering.

color.description: Optional: Color for the label in hex format (e.g., "#FF0000" for red, "#00FF00" for green). Used for visual distinction in UI.

project_id.description: Optional: Project ID to associate label with specific project (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). If omitted, label is global. Get from get_projects.

tools.name: get_pinned_items
tools.description: Fetches all pinned items in a project. Pinned items are shortcuts to important tasks, notes, or files displayed prominently for quick access. Use this to see what team members have pinned as important or frequently accessed. Essential for understanding project priorities.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tools.name: pin_item
tools.description: Pins a task, note, or file to the top of a project for quick access. Pinned items appear prominently for all project members. Use this to highlight important tasks, reference documentation, or frequently needed files. Useful for team coordination and prioritization.

projectId.description: Unique project identifier (numeric string, e.g., "197352"). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

type.description: Type of item to pin: "task" (pin a task), "note" (pin documentation), or "file" (pin an attachment)

item_id.description: ID of the item to pin (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_all_tasks, get_note, or get_all_files depending on type.

link.description: Optional: Custom link URL for the pinned item (e.g., external documentation URL)

tools.name: delete_pinned_item
tools.description: Removes a pinned item from a project. Use this to unpin tasks, notes, or files that are no longer priority or frequently accessed. Does not delete the underlying item (task/note/file), only removes the pin. Get pinned item IDs from get_pinned_items.

pinnedItemId.description: Unique pinned item identifier (numeric string, e.g., "12345"). Get from get_pinned_items response.

tools.name: get_all_states
tools.description: Fetches all available task states in Freelo. States represent task lifecycle status (e.g., 1=active/open, 2=finished/completed, 3=archived). Essential for understanding state IDs before using get_all_tasks with state_id filter or when analyzing task workflows. Returns state IDs, names, and descriptions.

tools.name: search_elasticsearch
tools.description: Performs powerful full-text search across Freelo using Elasticsearch. Searches through tasks, subtasks, projects, tasklists, files, and comments with advanced filtering options. Essential for finding content when you don't know the exact location. Supports filtering by projects, tasklists, authors, workers, states, entity types, and pagination. Much more powerful than get_all_tasks search_query for cross-entity searches.

search_query.description: Search query text (e.g., "urgent bug", "client meeting", "API documentation"). Searches across names, descriptions, and content.

projects_ids.description: Filter by project IDs (numeric array, e.g., [197352, 198000]). Get from get_projects or get_all_projects.

tasklists_ids.description: Filter by tasklist IDs (numeric array, e.g., [12345, 67890]). Get from get_project_tasklists.

tasks_ids.description: Filter within specific task IDs (numeric array, e.g., [12345, 67890]). Useful for searching task content and subtasks.

authors_ids.description: Filter by author/creator user IDs (numeric array, e.g., [12345, 67890]). Get from get_users or get_project_workers.

workers_ids.description: Filter by assigned worker user IDs (numeric array, e.g., [12345, 67890]). Get from get_users or get_project_workers.

state_ids.description: Filter by states (string array, e.g., ["active", "finished", "archived", "template"]). Common: "active" (open tasks), "finished" (completed).

entity_type.description: Filter by entity type: "task", "subtask", "project", "tasklist", "file", or "comment". Omit to search all types.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starts at 0 (default: 0). Use for loading more results.

limit.description: Maximum results per page (default: 100). Control response size and performance.

searchData.description: Search data with query and filters
